title: task closes when its linked child disappeared with its process
requirement: A task whose linked child disappeared (its process died, the Host restarted, no subagent/end ever arrived) closes through the ordinary acceptance path: status done, result recorded, the child row marked settled, the role row freed, and the disappearance named - no force flag and no lost acceptance. The first read of a board in a process settles active rows whose children the runtime can prove it no longer holds.
steps: Red first: TASKBOARD_MODULE=.dsh/red-first/taskboard.mjs node --test plugins/taskboard/test/dead-child-close.test.mjs (module materialised from git HEAD)
The close test writes a board row in review with one linked child the fake runtime roster does not hold, then calls the real service.close
The load test writes an active row with the same missing child and calls service.list once
expected: close returns ok with status done, the result kept, gone:[{childId,state:'gone'}], the child row sleeping and the role currentTaskId null; the first list settles the active row to review with a reconciled timeline entry naming the disappeared child. On the pre-fix module the close returns interrupt_failed with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading id)' and the sweep leaves the row active.
